title: Four eyes on the sky
caption: The Auxiliary Telescopes under the Magellanic Clouds, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The four Auxiliary Telescopes at ESO's Paranal Observatory point up at a night sky packed with things to see. Its dark, pristine skies make Paranal a leading spot on Earth for studying the Universe, and this picture shows just how much there is to look at.

To the right of the band of the Milky Way are two cloudy patches that look like bursts of galactic fireworks. They are the two Magellanic Clouds, Large and Small, dwarf galaxies held captive by the Milky Way's gravity.

In the Mapuche language of south-central Chile, the Magellanic Clouds are called lafken, labken or künchalabken, meaning the lagoons, as well as rünanko, meaning the water wells. The photograph was taken by Juan Carlos Muñoz Mateos, and it shows just how crowded the sky over Paranal can look on a dark night.

understand.summary: This is a landscape photograph taken with a camera at an ESO site, in visible light. The camera settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: A long camera exposure gathers far more light than the eye can, so the Milky Way and faint stars appear brighter and richer than they would to someone standing there.
